Night 8, Thursday, November 19. Everything happens in a single night. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} presents his motion before the Primogen, the Second Inquisition strikes if the coterie let the Thermometer climb too high, and the original of the File leaves the city on the last ferry. The coterie arrives with whatever it gathered in Parts 1 through 3. This part decides what each clue is worth.

The Order of the Night

Time Event Scene
Before midnight If the Thermometer is at 9 or higher: FIRSTLIGHT raid @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}
10:30 p.m. Primogen Council at Halloway Tower @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}
12:30 a.m. Mr. Pell leaves the tower with the briefcase @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}
12:55 a.m. Last ferry to Bainbridge from Colman Dock @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}
1:30 a.m. The ferry reaches the other shore Endings (@UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO]{Endings of the Climax})

If the Thermometer is below 9, A4-E02 doesn't happen and the night begins with the Council.

Before starting, the Storyteller reviews what the coterie brings. Each item adds to the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}).

Evidence Source Value at the Council
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.xQqepYpthm1bxP8u]{Halloway Knows About the Cold Water} · Halloway Knows About the Cold Water @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night} +1 die
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard} · The Inverted Guard @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”} +1 die
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.TOvLdg2zhgDzjOAG]{The Journals Bought in 1986} · The Journals Bought in 1986 @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.wQ2BqzruUybEIhSO]{A2-E04 · The Sheriff That Was} +1 die
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.wRvr7GFOMQsgTJ2z]{SEA-0411 Shipments / DOC-07} · SEA-0411 Shipments / @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411} @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} +2 dice (proves Halloway is ARCHER)
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.Pvm4xZpxzhCtg4rf]{Gale's Signature} · Gale's Signature @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} +1 die
“C.H.” email to Gale @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} +2 dice
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.c6hzsNRnUCcABsCZ]{Sal's Ledger} and @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.9WkqebVXUF2scLLC]{The Payment from Cascade Holdings} · Sal's Accounts and the Cascade Payment @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”}, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One} +1 die
@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German} · The German's Folios @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} +1 die (and the note “No. — C.H.”)
@UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978} · O'Connor's Letter @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.wQ2BqzruUybEIhSO]{A2-E04 · The Sheriff That Was} +1 die (and changes Marchetti's vote)
Witness: Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jXff6tMXQQbmJg0m]{Krell's Testimony}) @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} +3 dice
Witness: Lonnie Barras @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One} +2 dice
Witness: Dawson or Gale @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} +2 dice
Montgomery on their side @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers} +2 dice
The original drive in the coterie's hands @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} Halloway can't use it as evidence against the Prince

This scene comes first because, if it happens, it happens before the Council.

Storyteller Context

Only if the Thermometer reached 9. FIRSTLIGHT's Puget Cell, under Agent @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}, hits one of the three targets on ARCHER's list (@UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}). The Storyteller chooses the target based on where the coterie left the most traces:

Target When
The Harbor Island Hangar (@UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{The Harbor Island Hangar}) If ANOMALY logged the coterie several times or if FIRSTLIGHT has Lonnie or USB drive 3.
The Sheriff's Farm (@UUID[JournalEntry.NNzMhIvsavpG0iTQ]{The Sheriff's Farm and Boat Landing}) If the coterie is on the run after @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers} or if the hangar is empty.
The Prince's Penthouse in Capitol Hill If the coterie protected its havens well. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} prefers this target, because it exposes @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Whitmore} on the very night of the Council.

FIRSTLIGHT arrives at 9:40 p.m. with the tactical team (@UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team}): six operators in light body armor, with incendiary ammunition, high-intensity UV flashlights, a thermal camera drone, and a van carrying an artificial sunlight generator. Okafor directs from a car parked a block away. FIRSTLIGHT's goal is to capture a Kindred alive or, failing that, destroy it and take all the material.

If you played the FIRSTLIGHT interludes, check what they left before you start: @UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.8DXPPUEUUp5bHka5]{the advantages and cracks for the raid}. They change what each side brings to the door (the generator, the bullhorn, the drone, the exits), not who wins.

The coterie, or whatever part of it is at the target, has three priorities: get out alive, save the mortals (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear}, @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen}, the bounty hunters), and destroy whatever must not fall into FIRSTLIGHT's hands.

If it's the hangar:

The hangar's work lights flicker once and die. In the dark, you hear the whine of a drone right above the sheet-metal roof. Bear looks up from the workbench, sets down the pistol he was cleaning, and picks up another one, loaded. “Six,” he says, peering through a crack. “Two by the dock, four at the door. And a van that isn't police.” Under the big door, a white light starts creeping in, harsh, from no ordinary flashlight.

Tests

  • Spot the raid before it starts: Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 4). On a success, the coterie has two minutes before they breach. If someone has @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.qA75WygzgVjOeJvT]{LOR-03 · The City's Eyes} at level 5, they've known the target and the time since Night 7.
  • Destroy evidence: each item (the arsenal, the phones, the USB drive, Helen's papers) is Dexterity + Craft or Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 2) and takes one turn.
  • Resist the UV light: it isn't sunlight, but it burns. Each turn exposed: 1 aggravated damage. Fortitude (Defy Bane) reduces it.

Coterie Options

Option What Happens
Escape From the hangar: the cargo tunnel comes out 200 meters away, next to Terminal 46. Bear knows it. Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 3) for the whole group. The launch in the covered slip is another option, but the drone sees it: the Thermometer doesn't drop, but they escape. From the farm: the tunnel to the river landing. The dogs cover the retreat. At the Prince's penthouse: if the coterie isn't there, Whitmore escapes alone with Presence (Majesty) and arrives at the Council late and humiliated.
Manipulate There's no negotiating with FIRSTLIGHT mid-raid. But Bear can step out the door with his hands up, like a scared night watchman, and buy a minute: Bear's Manipulation + Performance (5 dice, Difficulty 3). If it works, the operators cuff him but don't go in yet. If Cole Ransom (@UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Cole Ransom}, @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade}) is on the team, he recognizes Bear: see Notes.
Combat The operators fight well and aren't afraid to die. Use the stats for @UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team} (chapter 8). Incendiary ammunition deals aggravated damage. Killing mortal operators: 1 Stain each, unless in direct defense of a mortal. A massacre hands FIRSTLIGHT the definitive proof: Thermometer 10 and a Purge.
Disciplines Obfuscate doesn't work against the drone's thermal camera, except with @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.qA75WygzgVjOeJvT]{LOR-03 · The City's Eyes} at level 4. Animalism: the farm dogs or the hangar rats attack the operators and create chaos. Dominate on an operator: it works, but Okafor sees everything through the body camera. Potence: knocking down the drone with a thrown object is Strength + Athletics (Difficulty 4). Without the drone, the team loses half its coordination.

Dialogue Guide: Agent Dana Okafor (by Radio or Bullhorn)

Forty-five, ex-FBI, calm voice. She believes what she hunts are monsters and that someone has to do it.

  • (By bullhorn) — “Homeland Security. Come out with your hands where we can see them. We know what you are. Nobody else has to get hurt.”
  • (To Bear, if he comes out) — “You the night watchman? Do you know who you work for, Mr. Whitman? Because we do.”
  • (If they capture a mortal and question them) — “We don't want the journalist. We want the file. And we want to know who's handing it to us. Because nobody gives away something like that.”

Consequences

  • The coterie escapes with everything destroyed: . FIRSTLIGHT is left with an empty building. The haven is burned: Haven −2 for its owner until they find another.
  • The coterie escapes but leaves evidence behind: no change to the Thermometer. FIRSTLIGHT has weapons, phones, or papers. Chronicle hook.
  • FIRSTLIGHT captures a mortal (Bear, Helen, a bounty hunter): the chronicle continues with a rescue. If it's Bear, @UUID[JournalEntry.5mQIPoGa4I0tQtbR]{Note Kept in Bear's Safe} comes into play.
  • FIRSTLIGHT captures a Kindred: Thermometer 10. Purge. The adventure ends in @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.on9MlxGjJpFF8yf2]{FIN-D · Red Tide} even if the Council goes well.

Storyteller Notes

  • Cole Ransom. If @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade} was triggered earlier, or if you want to introduce him now, @UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Ransom} is one of the six operators. When he sees Bear, he hesitates for half a second. That half second can save someone.
  • What Okafor doesn't know: that ARCHER is using her. If someone tells her over the radio, “Your source is a Ventrue who wants the crown,” Okafor doesn't believe it, but she writes it down. Chronicle hook.
  • Survivors of the raid arrive at the Council late, wounded, or with high Hunger. Keep that in mind.

Storyteller Context

Night 8, 10:30 p.m. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} has convened the Primogen with a formal petition: an “emergency regency” that temporarily sets the Prince aside for the duration of “the Second Inquisition crisis.” He can't depose @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Whitmore} on his own, but if a majority of the Primogen votes in favor, he can send the minutes to Justicar @UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Panhard}, who has been writing to him for a year. With a Justicar's blessing, the regency becomes a crown.

Halloway offered his tower (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}) “for security,” on the pretext that Elysium is too exposed to the cameras. Holding the Council in his own house is already a small victory. If the coterie managed to help the Prince regain the initiative (for example, by warning him ahead of time with evidence), the Council moves to the Glass Gallery (@UUID[JournalEntry.iyojT7kJHH23BWLd]{The Glass Gallery (Elysium)}) and Halloway loses 2 dice on all his rolls in the scene.

Present: Prince Whitmore, the five Primogen (Halloway, @UUID[JournalEntry.bB0eDKVFcxQW4C2d]{Marchetti}, @UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Voight}, @UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Thornquist}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.AeAhHuCNHL9KWVnT]{Fry}), Sheriff @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} (if he isn't at odds with the coterie), the coterie (summoned by the Sheriff, or sneaked in if it's on the run), and, standing behind Halloway, @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden} or her NPC substitute and @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}.

The private elevator climbs forty-two floors without a sound. It opens onto an enormous room with a single wall of glass over Elliott Bay: the harbor cranes, the ferry lights, the island where the Hound lives, all of it small, all of it still. In the center stands a long table of dark wood with seven chairs. Halloway stands at its head, hands clasped behind his back. He doesn't smile. On the table, in front of each chair, lies a closed folder with a name on it. When the Prince enters, Halloway inclines his head exactly as far as required. “Your Highness. Thank you for coming. This city has a problem, and I believe you know what it is.”

How the Scene Works

The Council has three stages: the motion (Halloway presents his case), the debate (the coterie and the others respond), and the vote.

1 · The Motion

Halloway speaks for five minutes without interruption. His case:

  • The Second Inquisition has a source inside the court (true: it's him).
  • That source has leaked three havens, all in the Prince's and the Sheriff's circle (true).
  • There's a killer on the docks who fights like the Hound's sire, and the Hound has met with him in secret (half true). He shows the drone footage.
  • The Prince received a warning from Regent Voight and didn't read it for two nights (true).
  • The Inquisition's source has been identified: the deliveries were paid for through Cascade Holdings. And then he opens the folder marked “C. Arden.”

Celeste's sacrifice. Halloway accuses his own childe of being ARCHER, with her signature on the accounts as proof. He does it with rehearsed sorrow: “This pains me more than anyone.” He asks the Primogen to hand her over to the Sheriff. That way he clears himself and shows he's willing to sacrifice his own “for the Masquerade.”

If Celeste is a PC, give the player a moment before you go on. See Notes.

2 · The Debate

The coterie responds. Whoever speaks for it makes the case roll:

Manipulation + Politics (Difficulty 4) or Charisma + Politics (Difficulty 4), +1 die for each piece of evidence on the checklist. Halloway answers with his own pool ( Halloway: Manipulation + Politics (10 dice)). It's a contested test. The margin decides:

Coterie's margin Result
Halloway wins The room believes him. Celeste is handed over. The votes lean toward the regency (see the vote, unchanged).
Tie or 1–2 successes Doubt. Nobody fully believes anybody. The vote decides.
3–4 successes Halloway is exposed. The vote almost certainly turns against him.
5 or more Total exposure. The Prince orders the Sheriff to arrest Halloway on the spot. Halloway flees: see Notes and @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}.

3 · The Vote

Halloway needs 3 votes in favor out of 5. Each Primogen has a default vote and a condition that changes it:

Primogen Default vote Changes to “no” if...
Halloway Yes Never.
Voight Yes. She believes Whitmore failed. The coterie proves to her that ARCHER is Halloway (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.wRvr7GFOMQsgTJ2z]{SEA-0411 Shipments / DOC-07}, the C.H. email, or Gale's or Dawson's testimony).
Thornquist Yes. Halloway paid him. The coterie proves to him that Krell, Halloway's man, destroyed Pike, his errand runner (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.hBCw4YOXRWH4DQhg]{The Controlled Fury Technique} plus @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jXff6tMXQQbmJg0m]{Krell's Testimony} or Krell's testimony). Or offers him something better: a bigger favor from the whole coterie.
Marchetti Abstains. She sees @UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978}, with Whitmore's note (“C.H. — watch”), or the coterie cites her record from Night 3 (@UUID[JournalEntry.lcO0CdwUlZHg2wAX]{Register of the Keeper of Elysium, November Folio}). Then she votes “no”: the record is what she respects most.
Fry Unpredictable: roll 1 die; even, yes; odd, no. Someone speaks a hard truth aloud during the debate. For example, a PC revealing that Krell is David's brother (or David saying it, if a PC convinced him), Hal admitting to his reports, or Celeste admitting she signed without looking. Then Fry votes with whoever spoke that truth.

By default, if the coterie does nothing, Halloway wins 3 to 0, with two abstentions or one Fry vote against.

Coterie Options

Option What Happens
Escape If the coterie is on the run and Halloway gives the order, the security ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) try to detain @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}, and getting him out is up to the coterie. Leaving the tower: the private elevator (requires Halloway's or Pell's key) or the emergency stairs (forty-two floors; Stamina + Athletics (Difficulty 3) to avoid reaching the bottom at Hunger 5).
Manipulate The case roll and the vote are the core. Also:
Negotiate with Halloway before the Council, in private: Halloway makes the coterie the offer, because he knows who's deciding things this week. For David, the office of Sheriff. For the whole coterie, domain over Harbor Island and Status 2. David listens and says nothing in front of Halloway. If the coterie accepts, David goes along. See @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}.
Have Nadia speak for the Prince: if @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia} is a PC, Whitmore asks her to speak on his behalf. She uses Charisma + Performance instead of Politics, and on a success it adds +2 dice to the case roll.
Combat Attacking Halloway in his tower, in front of the Primogen, is a breach of the Traditions and proves him right: “You see what I was telling you?” The vote goes “yes” automatically. It's only an option if Halloway is already exposed and fleeing.
Disciplines Halloway has Dominate 4 and Presence 3. If he feels he's losing, he uses Daunt on whoever is speaking for the coterie. Using Dominate on a Primogen during the Council is a crime: if it's discovered ( Voight: Wits + Awareness (7 dice)), that Primogen's vote swings against whoever tried it. Fry's Auspex: if anyone lies in the room, Fry says aloud, “That isn't true.”

Dialogue Guide: Charles Halloway

  • “You're ARCHER.” — “A serious accusation, without evidence, in my own house.” He barely smiles. “Please, continue.”
  • (Faced with P-10 or the C.H. email) — Silence. Then, very calmly: “Documents obtained illegally from a mortal company. Since when does the Camarilla sit in judgment using the Inquisition's methods?”
  • (Faced with Krell's testimony) — “A sectless mercenary, with no acknowledged sire, who killed three of our own. That's your witness?” He looks at David. “Or is he your brother?” (If @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} testifies, Halloway loses his composure for the first time: one of his hands moves.)
  • (To Celeste) — “I'm sorry, my dear. The Masquerade comes before both of us.”
  • (If he loses) — He smiles. This time he means it. “Your Highness, it's been a pleasure. As always.” And he heads for the elevator.

Dialogue Guide: Marcus Whitmore

  • (If the coterie defends him well) — He rises slowly. His voice fills the room effortlessly (Presence 5). “Charles. Sixty-four years ago I watched your sire make the same mistake. He thought a good story was the same thing as the truth.” A pause. “Sheriff.”
  • (If the coterie fails) — He stares at the table for a long while. “Very well. The Primogen have spoken.” To David: “Thank you, Mr. Smith. I believe you arrived late. Again.”

Dialogue Guide: Ethan Montgomery

  • (If the Prince orders Halloway's arrest) — He says nothing. He moves. Out in the lobby, the dogs start to howl.
  • (If Halloway wins and Montgomery sided with the coterie) — He takes the list out of his pocket. Looks at it. Puts it away. “Not tonight.” To David: “But tonight ends sometime.”

Storyteller Notes

  • Celeste (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden}). This is her scene. She has three clear options, and all of them are good: defend herself with the truth (if she found @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.9WkqebVXUF2scLLC]{The Payment from Cascade Holdings} and the note from the prelude, she can prove she only signed what Pell handed her: +2 dice to the case roll, and her Blood Bond to Halloway breaks at that moment if the player spends 1 point of Willpower), accept the accusation to save the coterie (Halloway wins the vote but loses his childe forever), or side with her sire and accuse David herself (see @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}). Don't push her toward any of them.
  • The promise to O'Connor. If the coterie promised him they'd bring @UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978} before the Primogen, this is the moment. If they do, @UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{O'Connor} knows by the next day and becomes Allies 2 for whoever did it. If they don't, he knows that too.
  • If Halloway flees (total exposure or defeat in the vote), he takes the private elevator down to level −3, takes the briefcase out of the vault, and gives it to Pell, or carries it himself if nobody stops him. See @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}.
  • If Halloway wins, at 12:30 a.m. Pell leaves with the briefcase for the ferry to deliver the original to the Justicar's envoy on Bainbridge. It's the proof Panhard asked him for before recognizing the regency. See @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}.

Storyteller Context

Night 8, 12:55 a.m. The last ferry of the night to Bainbridge Island leaves Colman Dock (@UUID[JournalEntry.IDd94316DhSx3ptV]{The Ferry Terminal and the Last Ferry}). On board is the briefcase with the File: the original drive or, if the coterie has that, the server from @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}'s private archive with the scanned journals and the cold subject database. Who carries it and where depends on how the Council ended:

Council result Who's on the ferry What they want to do with the briefcase
Halloway won @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Pell}, with Dawson and two ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) Deliver it to Archon @UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Duval}, who waits on Bainbridge as the Justicar's envoy, as proof of the “crisis” that justifies the regency.
Halloway lost the vote Halloway himself, with Dawson, Pell, and two ghouls Get out of the city. If they catch up to him, plan B: hand it over to @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Okafor}, who's waiting on the other shore. If he goes down, Seattle goes down with him.
Halloway exposed (5+ successes) Halloway, alone with Dawson, fleeing Same as above, but more desperate.

The crossing takes 35 minutes. On board are about forty mortal passengers, a crew of six, and security cameras in the cabins. Any fight is a Masquerade breach in an enclosed space over the water.

Who else might show up:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell}, if he survived and reached 3 steps in @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}: he appears on the car deck to help @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} and, for David's sake, the coterie. If he didn't reach 3 steps, he appears to recover the folios, and he's an unpredictable third force.

The terminal is nearly empty under the fluorescents. A guard checks his phone; a coffee machine blinks beside an “out of order” sign. Outside, the last ferry of the night waits with every light on, like a four-story white building floating on black water. The horn sounds once, long. On the passenger ramp, an old man in a dark suit with an aluminum briefcase climbs slowly, leaning on the arm of an enormous man who glances back and sniffs the air.

Tests

  • Board without being seen by Dawson: Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 4) against his Dawson: Wits + Awareness (6 dice). Dawson smells Kindred: Obfuscate doesn't work against his nose, but the wind off the Sound does (+1 die if they approach from upwind).
  • Make it in time: if the coterie leaves Halloway Tower after 12:30 a.m., Dexterity + Drive (Difficulty 3) to reach Colman Dock before 12:55 a.m. On a failure, they have to catch the ferry by boat (Bear's, Salt's, or the hangar's).
  • Find the briefcase on board: Wits + Investigation (Difficulty 3). Pell is in the second-deck passenger cabin, by a window, with the briefcase cuffed to his wrist.

Coterie Options

Option What Happens

Dialogue Guide: Mr. Pell

Ninety-six, looks sixty. Soft, polite voice, a butler from another era. He has served a single master for more than sixty years.

  • “Give us the briefcase.” — “I'm sorry. It isn't mine.”
  • “Halloway is going to let you die.” — Silence. “Mr. Halloway has fed me since 1958.” A pause. “Though it's true he's been late with it lately.”
  • “What's inside?” — “Twelve years of a woman who watched. Seventy of a man who waited.” He looks at the water. “I typed up Mr. Vance's journals, you know. Three copies. There were sentences that made me weep.”
  • (If he hands over the briefcase) — “Tell the journalist I'm sorry about her apartment. It was very tidy.”

Editor's Note

Doc 13 said Pell has served Halloway since 1950 (“seventy years”); it was settled as 1958, the year of Halloway's Embrace (“more than sixty years”). The age of 96 and the appearance of 60 stand.
